centers.name: East Convenience Center
centers.address: 943A Doctor Richard G. Adams Dr, Nashville, TN 37207

hours: Tuesday–Saturday, 8:30 a.m.–4:30 p.m. Closed on Metro holidays.
rules: Bring a Tennessee driver's license that shows a Davidson County address.
Household (residential) material only — no commercial waste, and no vehicles with commercial advertising or commercial tags.
Payment: cash (not at Omohundro), check, or card. Cards carry a 2.8% fee, minimum $1.95. Prices are set by Metro and aren't negotiable.

fees.material: 3 bags of trash (30 gal max each) + 1 bulk item
fees.limits: 1 visit a day. Excludes mattresses, tires with rims, and construction debris
Up to 100 lbs a day, including 1 TV no wider than 80 inches; 1 computer system a month
Up to 15 gallons or 100 lbs per household a month; 1 visit a day
Part of the hazardous-waste drop-off. Omohundro also takes it (no fee posted); call to confirm Ezell Pike
Up to 2 cubic yards on Metro's fee table, but its bulky item page says 1, so call to confirm. 1 visit a day
Up to 2 visits a day; load can't exceed the truck bed
1 visit a day. No construction debris; no trailers over 12 ft; no cargo vans or trailers at Anderson Lane

fees.material: Brush, leaves and other yard waste
fees.where: Living Earth: 1511 Elm Hill Pike or 6401 Centennial Blvd
fees.limits: Davidson County residents; trailers are charged a fee; hours vary
Up to 1 extra per home. Curbside service is for single-family homes in the Urban Services District

fees.material: Replacement cart (lost, stolen or damaged beyond repair)
